newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder - working class vote not enough.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder - working class vote not enough.

text.p: A leader of Germany's Social Democrats (SPD) said on Saturday it was time the left-leaning party learned that it was not going to win elections any more by aiming its appeal at the working class.

Gerhard Schroeder, premier of the state of Lower Saxony and a top candidate to challenge Chancellor Helmut Kohl in next year's general elections, told Bild daily the SPD needed to become more flexible.
He said the SPD could learn from experiences in other countries such as in the United States and Britain. Both the Democratic party and the Labour party have won office by broading their appeal.
"We have to realise that we are not going to win any elections these days with the working class alone," Schroeder said.
Schroeder, who is on a 12-day trip to meet business leaders in the United States, said that Germany could learn a lot from the United States.

"In America every worker moves into another city on average once every seven years," Schroeder said. "Even if this sort of flexibility cannot be directly transferred to Germany, we still have to learn to adjust better and faster to new conditions.
"That is not just the case for workers, but also for employers and unions," Schroeder said.
Schroeder also said Germany's tax system was in urgent need of reform and that the states were ready to compromise with the government in order to reach an agreement.
The media-friendly and pro-business Schroeder has been compared by many commentators to Britain's Tony Blair, who led his newly-modernised Labour party to election victory last week.
Opinion polls consistently say Schroeder is the SPD's best chance of ousting Kohl, who has been in power since 1982.
